concepts.label: Lithosphere and tectonic plates
quotes: Earth's outer shell, the lithosphere, is broken into large slabs called tectonic plates.
The lithosphere includes the crust and the rigid top layer of the mantle.

concepts.label: Plates move on the asthenosphere
quotes: The plates float on the asthenosphere, a hotter, softer layer of the mantle that can flow very slowly.

concepts.label: Slow plate motion and Pangaea
quotes: Plates move only a few centimetres per year, roughly as fast as fingernails grow.
About 200 million years ago, the continents were joined in a single supercontinent called Pangaea, which then broke apart.

concepts.label: Continental drift
quotes: In 1912, Alfred Wegener proposed the idea of continental drift.
He pointed to matching coastlines and matching fossils on continents that are now far apart.

concepts.label: Types of plate boundaries
quotes: Scientists group plate boundaries into three types.
At divergent boundaries, plates move apart and new crust forms as magma rises;
At convergent boundaries, plates move towards each other;
At transform boundaries, plates slide past each other sideways;

concepts.label: Hotspots are not plate boundaries
quotes: A hotspot is not a type of plate boundary: it is a plume of hot mantle rising under the middle of a plate, as under Hawaii.

concepts.label: Oceanic-continental subduction
quotes: When an oceanic plate meets a continental plate, subduction follows a typical order.
the denser oceanic plate bends downward beneath the continental plate.
water released from the sinking plate helps nearby mantle rock melt into magma.
the magma rises and can erupt to form a line of volcanoes on the continent.

concepts.label: Earthquakes and volcanoes at plate boundaries
quotes: Most earthquakes and volcanoes occur along plate boundaries.
The Ring of Fire around the Pacific Ocean is a belt of frequent earthquakes and volcanoes caused by subduction.
